config.title: Build typed pub sub bus

intro.title: Build typed pub sub bus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed publish-subscribe (pub/sub) bus in TypeScript, a pattern that allows different parts of an application to communicate by sending and receiving messages. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's generics and type safety to ensure that events are published and subscribed to with the correct data types. The main constructs involved include interfaces for defining event types, a central bus object to manage subscriptions, and functions for publishing events and subscribing to them. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe event system that prevents common runtime errors.
intro.usecase: A typed pub/sub bus is a foundational pattern for managing communication between decoupled components in large-scale applications. For example, in a financial dashboard, a stock price update published by a data feed service can be broadcast to multiple independent UI panels—like a chart, a ticker, and a summary widget—without them directly knowing about each other. This pattern is also essential in e-commerce sites, where adding an item to the cart (an event) needs to synchronize the cart modal, header badge, and checkout panel instantly. As a developer, implementing a typed pub/sub system ensures that events are safely structured and subscribers only receive data they expect, reducing bugs in complex, interactive UIs.

objectives: Implement a TypeScript interface to define the structure of a typed pub/sub bus.
Construct a class that initializes and manages typed event subscriptions.
Apply generic type parameters to create type-safe publish and subscribe methods.
Manipulate internal data structures to store and retrieve typed event handlers.
Integrate the pub/sub bus into a simple TypeScript module for testing.
Control the flow of typed events by publishing data to specific subscribers.
Configure the bus to handle multiple event types with distinct payloads.

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and interfaces
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript file and define the basic type structure for our pub/sub bus by declaring an interface for subscribers and a generic type for events.
steps.hint: Start by creating an interface for subscriber functions and a generic type for events that will carry data.

// Define the basic type structure for our pub/sub bus

steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an interface for subscriber functions and a generic type for events defined in TypeScript.
successCriteria: An interface named Subscriber and a generic type named Event are defined with proper TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined both the Subscriber interface and Event generic type with proper TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The types aren't defined correctly. Remember to create a Subscriber interface for callback functions and an Event generic type that can carry different data types.

steps.title: Define the EventHandler type
steps.instruction: Define a generic EventHandler type that accepts any payload type. Use TypeScript's generic syntax with a type parameter (e.g., <T>) and specify it as a function type that takes a payload of that type and returns void.
steps.hint: Think of EventHandler as a template for functions that handle events. The type should be something like: type EventHandler<T> = (payload: T) => void;
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a generic EventHandler type that can be used to type event-handling functions with any payload type.
successCriteria: A generic EventHandler type is defined with a type parameter and a function signature that takes a payload of that type and returns void.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your EventHandler type is generic (uses a type parameter like <T>) and defines a function that takes a payload of that type and returns void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The EventHandler type is not correctly defined. It should be a generic type that describes a function accepting a payload and returning void.

steps.title: Define the EventMap interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named EventMap that will map event names (as string keys) to their payload types (as values).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and curly braces. Inside, define key-value pairs where keys are strings and values are types.
steps.expectedOutcome: An EventMap interface is created to define the structure for event name to payload type mappings.
successCriteria: The EventMap interface is defined with a string index signature mapping to any type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the interface is named EventMap and uses a string index signature.
steps.feedbackWrong: The EventMap interface is not correctly defined. It should be an interface with a string index signature mapping to any type.

steps.title: Create the PubSubBus class skeleton
steps.instruction: Create a class named PubSubBus with a generic type parameter T that extends EventMap.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword followed by the class name and generic type parameter. Remember to add the constraint using the extends keyword.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PubSubBus class skeleton with proper generic constraint will be created.
successCriteria: The code contains a class named PubSubBus with a generic type parameter T that extends EventMap.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your class has the correct name and the generic type parameter properly extends EventMap.
steps.feedbackWrong: The class definition doesn't match the requirements. Check that you used the correct class name and generic constraint.

steps.title: Initialize the handlers storage
steps.instruction: Inside the PubSubBus class, add a private property named 'handlers' with the type 'Map<keyof EventMap, Set<EventHandler<any>>>' and initialize it as an empty Map.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript's private modifier and the Map constructor to create an empty map that will store event handlers by event name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PubSubBus class will have a properly typed private property to store event handlers, ready for the subscribe and unsubscribe methods.
successCriteria: The PubSubBus class contains a private 'handlers' property with the correct Map type and initialization.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the property is private, has the correct Map type with generics, and is initialized as a new Map.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handlers property is missing or has incorrect typing. Review the EventHandler and EventMap types to construct the proper Map type.

steps.title: Implement the subscribe method
steps.instruction: Inside the PubSubBus class, add a public subscribe method that accepts an event name (string) and a handler function, and stores the handler in the handlers map.
steps.hint: The method should be generic to capture the event type. Use the EventMap interface to type the event name and handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PubSubBus class will have a subscribe method that can register event handlers with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: The subscribe method is defined inside the PubSubBus class, accepts an event name and handler as parameters, and adds the handler to the handlers map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the method is inside the class, accepts both parameters, and stores the handler in the handlers map.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscribe method is missing or incorrectly implemented. Check the method signature and storage logic.

steps.title: Implement the unsubscribe method
steps.instruction: Inside the PubSubBus class, add an unsubscribe method that removes a specific handler for a given event type. The method should accept an event type (string) and a handler function, find the handler in the array, and remove it.
steps.hint: You can use the handlers map to get the array for the event type, then filter out the handler to remove. Make sure to handle cases where the event type doesn't exist.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PubSubBus class now has an unsubscribe method that can remove a specific handler from the internal storage.
successCriteria: The unsubscribe method is defined inside the PubSubBus class, accepts an event type and handler, and removes that handler from the handlers map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the unsubscribe method, but check the implementation. Make sure it properly removes the handler from the array for the given event type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The unsubscribe method is missing or incorrect. Remember to define it inside the class and implement the removal logic.

steps.title: Implement the publish method
steps.instruction: Inside the PubSubBus class, implement the publish method that accepts an event name and payload,
steps.hint: The publish method should retrieve the handlers array for the given event name from the handlers map, then iterate through each handler and call it with the payload.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PubSubBus class will have a publish method that can trigger all handlers for a specific event with the provided payload.
successCriteria: The publish method is implemented inside the PubSubBus class, accepts an event name and payload, retrieves handlers from the map, and calls each handler with the payload.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a publish method, but it might be missing proper type handling or the iteration logic. Make sure it retrieves handlers from the map and calls each one with the payload.
steps.feedbackWrong: The publish method is not implemented correctly. Check that it's inside the PubSubBus class, accepts event and payload parameters, and calls all handlers for that event.

steps.title: Create a usage example interface
steps.instruction: Define an example EventMap interface with specific event types and payloads to demonstrate real-world usage of your typed pub/sub bus.
steps.hint: Create a new interface that extends or implements your generic EventMap with concrete event names and payload types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a concrete EventMap interface with specific event names and typed payloads that demonstrates how the pub/sub bus can be used in real scenarios.
successCriteria: An example EventMap interface is defined with at least two different event types and their corresponding payload types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining an interface, but make sure it includes specific event names as keys and typed payloads as values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The example EventMap interface wasn't properly defined. Remember to create an interface with event names as keys and their payload types as values.

steps.title: Instantiate and use the typed pub/sub bus
steps.instruction: Create an instance of PubSubBus with your example EventMap interface and demonstrate usage by subscribing to an event, publishing a payload, and logging the result.
steps.hint: Instantiate the class with new PubSubBus<YourEventMap>(), then call subscribe with an event name and handler, and publish with matching event name and payload.
steps.expectedOutcome: A fully typed pub/sub bus instance is created and used with proper TypeScript type checking for events and payloads.
successCriteria: PubSubBus is instantiated with ExampleEvents type, subscribe is called with a valid event name and handler, and publish is called with matching event name and typed payload.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the ExampleEvents interface when creating the PubSubBus instance and that your subscribe/publish calls match the event names and payload types defined in that interface.
